title: Product Management Considerations
coreMove: Treat project outputs as entries in a longer product life: name the owner, connect roadmap choices to feedback, and measure value after closure.

exampleSpecs.stakes: avoid handing over an output with no continuing owner
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a small observed moment shows the product lifecycle extending beyond project closure

exampleSpecs.audience: teams whose delivery metrics hid adoption problems
exampleSpecs.stakes: locate the misstep that stranded product value after delivery
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: open after the failure and identify the missed roadmap/backlog decision

exampleSpecs.audience: project leads moving products across platforms
exampleSpecs.stakes: correct an ownerless handoff before migration work closes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist notices his own lifecycle error mid-stream

exampleSpecs.audience: sponsors deciding how project scope connects to product work
exampleSpecs.stakes: put continuing prioritization into the written artifact
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the written memo carries the scene and the action

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders comparing project-scope and product-priority habits
exampleSpecs.stakes: show how opposite backlog habits change outcomes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two named people face the same roadmap/backlog situation with divergent results

exampleSpecs.audience: teams ready to treat delivery as the end
exampleSpecs.stakes: reframe closure as a handoff into product life
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a peer gives a quotable reframe about lifecycle ownership
